sources.publisher: Universidad de los Andes / Congreso Visible
sources.title: Francia Elena Márquez Mina: birth, education and public-office chronology
sources.findings: Read the Universidad de los Andes Congreso Visible profile. It gives the full name Francia Elena Márquez Mina, birth on 1 December 1981 in Suárez, law graduation in 2020, and office history. Its generic congresista page template does not establish that she served in Congress: it explicitly has no corporation or constituency. Its ministerial end date of 26 February 2025 conflicts with the later official handover report; use the report’s 3 March departure, distinguishing the 27 February public announcement. The profile ends her vice-presidential period on 6 August 2026, whereas the post-term interview calls 7 August the administration’s last day; record the 7 August transition, without implying an additional term. Creative-writing study begun in 2021 is not a verified completed qualification.

sources.title: Alumna Francia Márquez: graduation from the law programme in 2020
sources.findings: Read the university’s alumni article. It directly confirms graduation from its law programme in 2020 and origin in Suárez. The page displays 3 May 2023 but describes the 2022 election tickets as forthcoming; do not date the election from that publication field. Its promotional language and statements about the other three alumni are not transferred to Márquez. A law qualification is not a research doctorate, and no credential document or honorary-degree award ceremony was independently inspected.

sources.title: 2018 South and Central America recipient: La Toma campaign and women’s march
sources.findings: Read the Goldman recipient biography, including the background, November 2014 march, December agreement, equipment removal by the end of 2016 and continuing pollution. The award is for South and Central America in 2018; it is not a Nobel Prize. The page’s introduction says 350 miles but its detailed body says 350 kilometres, so omit a precise distance rather than silently resolve the contradiction. It reports about 80 women and ten days of walking, followed by 22 days of protest; these are not the same duration. Describe the campaign’s historic local outcome with attribution, not an enduring end to all illegal mining or water contamination. Its then-current law-student and congressional-candidate descriptions are historical, not current 2026 offices. Do not infer success in the 2018 congressional election.

sources.title: 23 March 2022: Petro announces Márquez as his running mate
sources.findings: Read Caracol Radio’s 23 March 2022 report confirming the running-mate announcement and second place in the Historic Pact primary of 13 March. Second place is within that coalition’s primary, not the eventual presidential election or all coalitions combined. The article’s dynamic November 2026 site header is not the event date. Proposed campaign headquarters and registration deadlines are prospective statements, not independently verified later actions. No exact primary vote total or recording transcript is adopted.

sources.publisher: Congress of Colombia / Gaceta del Congreso 1063
sources.title: Record of the 7 August 2022 session: vice-presidential oath, published 12 September
sources.findings: Read the opening of the congressional record and the actual vice-presidential oath passage on printed page 15. The sitting was 7 August 2022; 12 September is the gazette’s publication date. Petro administered Márquez’s oath after his own inauguration. The form of address doctora in the proceedings is not evidence of an earned doctoral degree. Only the relevant session metadata and oath passage were checked; no claim to have audited every participant, speech or vote in the gazette.

sources.title: 30 June 2023: first equality and equity minister sworn in at Manaure
sources.findings: Read Infobae’s account of the completed ministerial oath at Manaure on 30 June 2023. The URL is dated 1 July, while the article timestamp and body give the 30 June event; use the event date. She was the first holder of the ministry and remained vice-president. The stated population remit and policy objectives are not measured results. Political criticism of cost and bureaucracy remains attributed; no exact budget-execution or spending conclusion is derived from the announcement.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Equality and Equity, Colombia
sources.title: Márquez’s handover report: designation, ministry establishment and departure on 3 March 2025
sources.findings: Read the official handover report’s initial identification fields and institutional-establishment narrative. It identifies 29 June 2023 as designation/start of management and 3 March 2025 as departure. The 4 January law created the ministry; June regulations and designation are different from the 30 June oath. Its account of legal, administrative and operational construction is the outgoing minister’s report, not an independent evaluation of every programme, contract or budget. Only those relevant introductory sections were reviewed, not all 7,634 extracted lines. No current legal existence of the ministry is inferred from the historical report.

sources.title: 27 February 2025 dispatch: Petro announces replacement of the equality minister
sources.findings: Read the EFE dispatch from Bogotá dated 27 February 2025, published by SWI on 28 February. It confirms Petro’s public announcement of Rosero as replacement and publicly reported disagreements within the government. That announcement date must not displace the 3 March departure in the official handover document. Its statement that she resigned is not independently resolved against later reporting that no resignation letter had been presented; the profile uses neutral departure language. Allegations involving other officials are not findings against Márquez.

sources.title: 3 March 2025 decree appoints Carlos Rosero; distinction from earlier cabinet announcement
sources.findings: Read Infobae’s 4 March 2025 report about Decree 0251 signed on 3 March, appointing Carlos Rosero and replacing the earlier ministerial appointment. Distinguish the reported decree from the earlier cabinet presentation and from leaving the elected vice-presidency. The article’s characterization of the legal mechanism and assertions about her intentions are not adopted as definitive legal findings. The embedded decree image and original government decree were not visually or separately reviewed; the handover document corroborates the departure date.

sources.title: 21 August 2026 interview: former vice-president reviews her term and discusses future plans
sources.findings: Read Cambio’s 21 August 2026 report of that day’s interview, both its accessible distribution-host copy and the canonical page’s relevant text. It identifies her as former vice-president, describes the 7 August end of the administration and supplies direct recent personal-activity evidence. Her statements on racism, political disputes and shortcomings in government are her account; they are not judicial determinations or an independently audited causal account of disaster deaths. Her plans for memoirs, philanthropy and a foundation are intentions, not completed publications, funding commitments or a registered organisation. The interview video and the underlying documents she criticised were not reviewed. Do not infer that the ministry’s entire subsequent legal history has been audited from this interview.

sources.title: 28 September 2026: possible Cali mayoral bid explicitly remains unconfirmed
sources.findings: Read El País Cali’s 28 September 2026 report on a possible 2027 mayoral bid, including its canonical page and distribution copy. It explicitly says the claim is unconfirmed, so no formal candidacy, election victory or new office is asserted. The article wrongly describes her as holding the equality ministry for all four years; the official 2025 handover and 2023 inauguration override that wording. Older photo captions and a dynamic November site header are not fresh personal appearances. Polling figures are omitted because the underlying survey was not reviewed. The report supports a dated caution, not proof of present-day activity or absence of later developments.

sources.title: 2023 academic council record: appended biographical CV and honorary-degree nomination
sources.findings: Read the appended biographical CV in the 13 September 2023 UPN academic-council record. It independently supports birth on 1 December 1981 in Suárez and childhood in Yolombó, with farming and artisanal gold extraction. A few secondary biographical search results instead give 1982; use the corroborated university records and retain the discrepancy here. This is an honorary education doctorate nomination, not proof of completion of a research PhD or of a later award ceremony. The adjacent heading’s Helena spelling is not preferred to the full Elena form in congressional and government records. The source’s 2005 reference to 35 years since dam construction is internally questionable and unused; no original 2010 court judgment was read or quoted.

portraitReview.license: Public Domain Mark — photographer account designation; project suitability pending
portraitReview.credit: FotoPresidencia Colombia; cropped version uploaded by Chien
portraitReview.unresolved: Read Commons crop and full parent record and the original Flickr entry. Flickr records capture and upload on 29 January 2023. Chien uploaded the 6000×4000 parent at 06:06 and 899×1163 crop at 06:09 on 9 July 2023; these are not the capture date. The parent records FlickreviewR 2 confirmation of Public Domain Mark on 9 July 2023. The Flickr account currently appears as Archivo fotográfico presidente Gustavo Petro 2022–2026 / REPÚBLICA DE COLOMBIA, while Commons credits FotoPresidencia Colombia. The mark is a public-domain designation, not a CC BY licence or an automatic rule that all Colombian government photographs are public domain; confirm provenance and suitability under the project’s use requirements. The crop description identifies Márquez and the parent says she is between two farmers, but no pixels were inspected. Original download on 18 November returned curl 22, HTTP 403 and reported HTTP 000. Referenced cached JPEG is absent. Identity, colour, crop correspondence and resolution still require visual verification.
